newsitem.title: USA: Abducted schoolgirls back at home in Michigan.
newsitem.headline: Abducted schoolgirls back at home in Michigan.

text.p: Two young sisters who were abducted and driven to Florida in a four-day ordeal were back home with their family in Michigan Tuesday night after police found them and arrested the three men who took them.

Clutching large teddy bears and wearing FBI and sheriff's department baseball caps, Teresa Hainer, 9, and Jessica Hainer, 6, stepped off a private jet in Kalamazoo with their father, Jesse Hainer, of nearby Galesburg, Michigan.

The girls disappeared last Friday when they hopped off a school bus and got into a station wagon with three men. They were the subject of a nationwide search involving thousands of law enforcement officials which ended Tuesday morning in Daytona Beach, Fla.
"I'm just glad my girls weren't hurt real bad," Jesse Hainer told reporters in Daytona. "I get to take them home. I hope this never happens to anybody else in their family."
FBI Special Agent Joseph Martinolich said at a news conference earlier Tuesday that the girls were "maybe a little tired, a little bedraggled, maybe dishevelled, but they're in good shape."

Police in Daytona Beach arrested the three suspects -- acquaintances of the girls' father -- without incident about 9:30 a.m. (1430 GMT) as they entered a store with the girls on the beach town's main commercial strip.
A college missionary from Cambridge, Mass., spoke to the suspects and the girls at length Monday and later that night called police after she recognised their pictures on television newscasts.
"I met them out on the beach. They looked kind of scruffy," said Loh-Sze Leung, 20, a Harvard University student who was in Daytona with an evangelical group.
"The girls seemed kind of unhappy or shy. But nothing seemed wrong. They didn't look like they were on the run or anything," she said.

Ronald Stafford, 21, his brother Lee Stafford, 17, and Ricky Geer, 19, were arrested on federal kidnapping charges. They also will be charged with kidnapping under Michigan state law, which will allow Lee Stafford to be tried as an adult.
Court records showed that Ronald Stafford spent three years in an adolescent sex-offender programme.
Martinolich said the men made no demand for money and their motive for abducting the girls is still "in the realm of speculation."
Geer told reporters as he was being led to a police van for transport to a federal detention centre that he did not know the girls had been kidnapped.
Asked why the men had the girls, Geer said, "I don't know. I was picked up downtown (in Kalamazoo) and I was asked if I wanted to go to Florida. As far as I know, it was Ron's daughters."

Olivia Hainer, the girls' grandmother, thanked the "G-men" who located Teresa and Jessica and said she planned a big welcome home celebration for them. The girls' father is divorced from their mother but has full custody of them.

The two schoolgirls were supposed to go to a babysitter's home when they were dropped off at a Galesburg trailer park on Friday afternoon, but a man waiting for the bus told them to get into a 1988 Pontiac 6000 station wagon instead.
Police and witnesses said the girls at first did not want to go, but eventually got into the car anyway.
